modes.cue_notes: Sit with legs spread wide apart. Allow the spine to round forward in a C-curve and walk the hands forward between or beyond the legs. Head hangs. Feel the inner thighs, hamstrings, and posterior spine receiving the stretch. Do not force the legs wider — gravity does the work over time. Can also fold toward each leg individually to target one hamstring at a time.

source: Traditional yin yoga; see Paul Grilley, Bernie Clark, Sarah Powers
notes: Targets the inner thigh (adductors), hamstrings, and posterior spinal ligaments. Kidney and bladder meridians run the back line; liver meridian runs the inner thigh.

breathing_cues.entering: Inhale to sit tall with legs wide, then on a slow exhale walk the hands forward and allow the spine to drape forward in a long C-curve. Let the inner thighs and posterior spine receive the weight of the torso.
breathing_cues.holding: Breathe easily. With each exhale, release any gripping in the inner thighs and lower back. Visualize the adductor fascia softening and lengthening without any muscular effort pulling the legs apart.
breathing_cues.exiting: On an inhale, walk the hands back toward the pelvis and press up to sitting, then bring the legs slowly together — one at a time — to avoid strain on the sacroiliac joints.

modifications.name: Legs Less Wide
modifications.description: Reduce the angle between the legs to a comfortable range — 60 to 90 degrees — so the inner thigh and hamstring receive a therapeutic load without overstretching the adductor attachments at the ischium.

modifications.name: Bolster in Front
modifications.description: Place a bolster lengthwise between the legs and rest the torso on it, allowing the body to fully surrender without muscular effort to hold the fold.

modifications.name: Sit on Blanket
modifications.description: Elevate the sitting bones on a folded blanket to reduce posterior pelvic tilt and allow the pelvis to tip forward, making the forward fold more accessible.

modifications.name: Unilateral Side Fold
modifications.description: Walk the hands toward one leg to fold over that side's hamstring and inner thigh, effectively turning the bilateral straddle into a half-dragonfly variation for targeted one-sided work.

emotional_release_potential.notes: The wide-legged position exposes the inner groin — an area associated with vulnerability, intimacy, and boundaries; the liver meridian runs this line.
Releasing held tension in the inner thighs and groin (kidney meridian territory) can dissolve stored fear and cultivate a sense of grounded confidence.
